I need to examine the issue repository, focusing on insertIssue, updateIssue, archiveIssue, and related functions.

I need to understand how notifications are triggered for status changes.

The notification service currently subscribes to issue.assigned, issue.overdue, comment.created, and member.joined. It does not yet subscribe to issue.status_changed or issue.archived.

A new `sub_issues_completed` notification kind will be added. It fires when a sub-issue closes and its parent is left with no open issues below it. The parent assignee receives this once, through the usual fan-out, respecting their preferences and excluding the changer.

The notification is suppressed when the parent has no assignee, is archived, or has no sub-issues. It also does not fire for non-closing changes such as reopening or moving a sub-issue. Reopening and re-closing a sub-issue will trigger the notice again. Only the direct parent is evaluated.

I need to determine whether archiving a parent issue triggers the completion notice on its assignee. The cascading archive of descendants may count as a sub-issue stopping being open.

Archiving a parent before its children would archive the parent first. The spec suppresses the completion notice when the parent is archived, so the notification would not fire.

The safest approach is to check the parent after each individual sub-issue archive. If the parent is still live and has an assignee, and no open descendants remain, the completion notice fires. Archiving a parent alongside its children would suppress the notice if the parent itself is archived first.

When archiving a subtree, the grandchild is archived alongside its parent. The direct parent of that grandchild is already archived, so no completion notice fires for it. The root parent still has no open issues below it, so its assignee should be notified.

The word "once" means one notification per closing transition that empties the subtree, not a single permanent alert. Reopening and re-closing a sub-issue will trigger the notice again. During a cascading archive, both the child and its parent stop being open.

Both the intermediate parent and the root parent may receive a completion notice during a cascading archive if each is left with no open descendants. The phrase "told once" likely means one notification per parent, not one total across the entire operation.

Closing multiple sub-issues in one cascade should trigger the parent notification exactly once, when the last open descendant closes. During a tree archive, each direct parent should be notified at most once if it is left with no open descendants and at least one was closed. The existing issue.archived event for each archived descendant remains separate.

The completion check should live in subscribers to `issue.archived` and `issue.status_changed`. Each archived child triggers a parent check. The first child archived may leave the parent with open descendants, so no notification fires. The last child archived leaves the parent empty, triggering exactly one completion notice.

Events must be emitted as each sub-issue is archived, not after the entire cascade finishes. If events are batched, a child's archive event may arrive after its parent is already archived, so the completion check would miss it.

The `issue.status_changed` subscriber can identify a closing transition by comparing `from` and `to` values. It then checks whether the direct parent has no open descendants remaining.

A status change from open to done or canceled counts as a closing transition that triggers the completion notice. Moving a closed issue to another closed status does not trigger it. Reopening a sub-issue also does not trigger it. Archiving an already-closed issue does not count as stopping being open.

Archiving an already-closed issue does not change the open count, so no completion notice fires. Archiving an open sub-issue that is not the last one also produces no notification, because its parent still has other open issues below it. Moving a sub-issue to a new parent via setIssueParent is handled separately.

Moving a sub-issue away from its parent does not trigger the completion notice, even if the parent is left with no open issues below it. Creating a new issue under a parent also does not count as a closing transition. An edge case remains where a sub-issue closes while another open descendant exists at a deeper level.

The completion notice fires only for the direct parent of the sub-issue that closes. A deeper open descendant prevents notification for that parent. The root is not notified until its own open child is closed.

The subscriber logic is now concrete. On `issue.status_changed`, it checks that the issue moved from open to closed, loads its parent, and skips if the parent is archived or has no assignee. It then counts non-archived descendants of the parent; if zero, it notifies the parent's assignee with kind `sub_issues_completed`. The `issue.archived` subscriber will load the archived issue.

The `issue.archived` event does not include status, so the subscriber must load the issue to confirm it was open before archiving. During a cascading archive, each child emits its own event; if the parent is also archived in that same cascade, the completion check for that child will be skipped.

The top issue in a cascading archive is handled correctly: its parent is still live, all descendants are archived, so the open count drops to zero and the parent gets notified once. If only one sibling subtree is archived while others remain open, the parent keeps an open count above zero and receives no notification. A potential double-notify scenario is flagged.

The potential double-notify concern is resolved. Each archived event checks only its own direct parent, so a parent is never notified twice during a cascade.

Archiving a single open sub-issue leaves the parent with other open descendants, so no completion notice fires. Closing that same sub-issue while another sibling remains open also produces no notification. The notice only triggers when the last open descendant closes.

Closing multiple siblings in separate calls works correctly: each one notifies its parent only after the prior sibling is closed.

If a sub-issue is archived while another sibling is already closed, the open count drops to zero and the parent receives exactly one notification.

Sub-issues may not exceed three levels deep. The root issue sits at level zero.

The maximum depth is three, so a four-level chain from root to great-grandchild is the limit. A move is judged by where its deepest descendant would land: if the parent sits at level L and the issue has a deepest descendant at depth D, the new position would be L+1+D, which must not exceed three.

The depth formula is being refined. A node with a child moved under a level-2 parent would land at level 4, exceeding the limit. The maximum relative depth of a descendant must be at most three minus the parent's level.

Moving an issue to root level always satisfies the depth limit because descendants shift up. The spec says a successful move or removal of a parent is announced as an issue.updated event with changedFields: ["parentId"]. If the parentId is unchanged, no such event should fire.

A move that leaves the parent unchanged should return the issue without emitting an event, consistent with how `changeIssueStatus` skips unchanged statuses. Cycle detection must reject any attempt to place an issue under itself or under one of its own descendants.

A parent must be a live issue in the same project. A parent from another project or workspace raises NotFoundError, and an archived parent raises AlreadyArchivedError. Creation with a parent follows the same rules: the parent must exist, be unarchived, and satisfy the depth limit. Because the new issue does not yet exist, cycle detection is only needed when the parent lookup fails.

Invalid parents during creation raise NotFoundError and emit no event. TenantScopeError applies to every operation when the orgId is outside the actor's workspace. setIssueParent, listSubIssues, getIssueRollup, and createIssue with a parent all require the target issue to exist in that workspace.

Moving an issue requires `issue:update` on that issue. Listing sub-issues and reading roll-ups require `issue:read` on the target issue. An archived issue cannot be moved. The `setIssueParent` flow is being structured to validate org scope, find the issue, assert update permission, reject archived issues, then resolve the parent, check for cycles, and enforce depth limits.

The parent itself is not checked for permissions beyond existence and same-project membership. Sub-issues move with their parent implicitly; they do not need reparenting, and the depth limit already accounts for them. The listSubIssues endpoint returns only direct, unarchived sub-issues ordered oldest first by creation time and then issue number.

The roll-up counts every descendant at any depth that is not archived. Open issues are those that are unarchived and not done or canceled. Closed issues are those that are unarchived and done or canceled. The total equals open plus closed. The parent issue itself is excluded from the count.

A parent with no sub-issues receives no completion notification. The thought cuts off while considering a scenario where a parent has one open child.

The completion notification is triggered only when the last open sub-issue closes. Archived sub-issues are excluded from the count, so a parent with only archived descendants has zero open sub-issues and does not receive a notification.

The phrase "for a parent without sub-issues" is ambiguous. It could mean the parent never had children, or that it currently has zero descendants after all were archived. The spec lists this as one of the cases where nothing is sent.

The phrase "for a parent without sub-issues" is interpreted as: do not notify the assignee of an issue that itself has no sub-issues when that issue is closed. Only the direct parent receives the completion notice.

Archiving the last open sub-issue must still trigger a completion notification for its parent. The parent may then have zero live sub-issues, but the spec explicitly requires this notification when an open issue is archived.

Archiving a sub-issue that is already closed does not trigger a completion notification, because the event only fires when an open issue stops being open. If every sub-issue of a parent is already closed, no notification is sent either.

The notification rule is finalized. A completion notice fires only when a closing occurs, the parent exists, the parent is live and has an assignee, and the open descendant count drops to zero. The "without sub-issues" clause applies only to issues that lack any parent.
